meta.title: India Jobs Market Visualizer
meta.subtitle: Karpathy-style treemap for India's 2024-2025 tech labour market
meta.methodology: Static, auditable dataset assembled from the provided India tech labour-market research. Areas are approximate workforce demand weights; colors are driven by selectable metrics. AI exposure is heuristic and indicates how much AI may reshape work, not whether a job disappears.
sources: NASSCOM Strategic Review 2025: tech industry revenue ~$282.6B and workforce ~5.8M
Naukri JobSpeak 2025: AI/ML hiring +25% to +54% YoY across months
GCC market summaries: 1,700+ centers, ~2.4M workers, six Tier-1 city concentration
Salary guides and public compensation aggregators referenced in the project research PDF

cities.specialization: Automotive tech, enterprise SaaS, industrial software

roles.title: AI Engineer
roles.rationale: Core work is digital and AI-assisted, but demand is expanding rapidly as companies build AI products. Exposure is high because tools reshape workflows, not because demand is weak.

roles.title: Machine Learning Engineer
roles.rationale: The job is software-heavy and model-centric, so AI automates experimentation and coding. Demand remains strong where ML systems must be deployed reliably.

roles.title: Data Scientist
roles.rationale: Analysis, reporting and modeling are almost entirely digital and increasingly automatable. The strongest roles shift toward product judgment, causal reasoning and stakeholder ownership.

roles.title: Data Engineer
roles.rationale: AI assists coding and pipeline generation, but production data reliability and platform context keep human ownership important.

roles.title: Big Data Testing Engineer
roles.rationale: Test generation and validation can be accelerated by AI, but enterprise data quality remains domain-specific and integration-heavy.

roles.title: Software Developer / SDE
roles.rationale: This is a fully digital occupation where coding assistants substantially change throughput. Demand may still rise because cheaper software creation expands the market.

roles.title: Full-Stack Developer
roles.rationale: Frontend and backend implementation are highly AI-assistable. Higher-value work moves toward architecture, product reasoning and security-aware delivery.

roles.title: Backend Engineer
roles.rationale: AI writes boilerplate and tests, but distributed-system reliability, performance and business rules remain harder to automate fully.

roles.title: Frontend Engineer
roles.rationale: UI generation is increasingly automated, making exposure very high. Differentiation shifts to design judgment, performance and product polish.

roles.title: Mobile App Engineer
roles.rationale: AI can generate common app screens and logic, but platform constraints, app quality and device testing keep the role moderately resilient.

roles.title: Product Manager
roles.rationale: Research, specs and analytics are AI-assisted, but prioritization, customer empathy and cross-functional influence require human judgment.

roles.title: UX / Product Designer
roles.rationale: Generative design tools produce variants quickly, increasing exposure. Senior designers remain valuable where user research and product taste matter.

roles.title: Cloud Engineer
roles.rationale: AI helps with IaC and troubleshooting, but cloud architecture, incidents and governance require accountable operators.

roles.title: DevOps Engineer
roles.rationale: Automation is intrinsic to the role and AI adds another layer. Production ownership and incident response keep exposure below pure digital content roles.

roles.title: Site Reliability Engineer
roles.rationale: AI improves diagnostics, but reliability work involves high-stakes systems, accountability and operational judgment.

roles.title: Cybersecurity Analyst
roles.rationale: AI automates triage and detection engineering, but adversarial dynamics and shortage of skilled professionals keep demand strong.

roles.title: Security Engineer
roles.rationale: AI helps attackers and defenders, increasing productivity but not eliminating expert review, architecture and accountability.

roles.title: ERP / Enterprise Consultant
roles.rationale: Documentation, configuration guidance and testing are AI-assistable, while client-specific implementation and change management remain human-heavy.

roles.title: QA / Test Automation Engineer
roles.rationale: AI can generate tests and detect regressions, making routine QA highly exposed. Strategic quality engineering remains valuable.

roles.title: IT Support Specialist
roles.rationale: Chatbots and self-healing tools reduce repetitive tickets, but physical device support and escalation handling remain necessary.

roles.title: BPO / Customer Support Associate
roles.rationale: Conversational AI can automate common support interactions. Complex escalation, empathy and regulated processes keep humans in the loop.

roles.title: Business Analyst
roles.rationale: AI drafts requirements and analyses data quickly, but stakeholder alignment and domain interpretation remain human-led.

roles.title: GCC Engineering Manager
roles.rationale: Managerial reporting is AI-assisted, but hiring, execution ownership, mentoring and stakeholder trust are harder to replace.

roles.title: Automotive Software Engineer
roles.rationale: Software components are AI-assistable, but safety, hardware integration and compliance lower exposure relative to web software.

roles.title: Embedded Systems Engineer
roles.rationale: Code generation helps, but hardware constraints, lab debugging and real-time reliability create a physical-world moat.

roles.title: VLSI / Semiconductor Engineer
roles.rationale: EDA workflows benefit from AI, but chip design requires deep verification, toolchain expertise and high-cost error prevention.

roles.title: Manufacturing Automation Engineer
roles.rationale: AI assists monitoring and maintenance, but plant-floor presence, equipment integration and safety reduce digital-only exposure.

roles.title: FinTech / BFSI Engineer
roles.rationale: Financial software is digital and AI-assisted, but compliance, auditability and domain risk limit full automation.

roles.title: Risk / Fraud Analyst
roles.rationale: Pattern analysis and report writing are highly automatable. Human review remains important for exceptions, regulation and accountability.

roles.title: Salesforce / CRM Developer
roles.rationale: AI accelerates configuration and code, while enterprise integrations and business-process nuance preserve demand.

roles.title: Technical Writer
roles.rationale: Drafting and summarization are core AI strengths. The surviving premium is in technical accuracy, structure and developer empathy.

roles.title: Digital Marketing Specialist
roles.rationale: Content, keyword research and campaign variants are highly automatable. Strategy, brand judgment and conversion ownership become more important.

roles.title: Content Moderator
roles.rationale: AI moderation handles common cases, but edge cases, local language nuance and policy escalation still require human reviewers.

roles.title: Tech Recruiter
roles.rationale: Sourcing, screening and scheduling are automatable, but closing candidates and understanding team fit remain relationship-driven.

roles.title: AI Startup Builder / Founder
roles.rationale: Founders use AI as leverage rather than face replacement. The role is defined by opportunity selection, distribution and execution risk.

roles.title: Solutions Architect
roles.rationale: AI helps create diagrams and proposals, but enterprise trust, context and accountable architecture decisions keep humans central.

roles.title: AI Agent Developer
roles.rationale: The role exists because of AI and uses AI heavily. Exposure is high, but market demand is currently expanding faster than automation pressure.
